conventions: TypeScript with ESM imports; match the style of the file being edited (single quotes, trailing commas, 2-space indent, 80-column Prettier wrapping); run Prettier on every changed file.
Never change the existing Apache 2.0 header or its year; a new .ts/.tsx file starts with the Apache 2.0 header with `Copyright 2026 The Backstage Authors`.

Schema walkers use the local `isObject(value): value is JsonObject` guard and `JsonObject` / `JsonValue` from `@backstage/types`; never mutate an input schema, build new objects with spread or Object.fromEntries.
Helpers added by this change are module-internal: do not add them to any `index.ts` barrel, `src/alpha.ts` or `src/index.ts`, and add no TSDoc release tag to them.
No new dependencies; use only `json-schema-library` (Draft07), `@rjsf/*` 5.24.13 and lodash already in plugins/scaffolder-react/package.json.
Tests run on Jest via `CI=1 yarn test <file>`; name cases `it('should ...')` inside the file's existing `describe`; prefer few thorough cases with several `expect`s each.

React tests: use `renderInTestApp` from `@backstage/test-utils` wrapped in `SecretsContextProvider` for Stepper, plain `render` from `@testing-library/react` for ReviewState; query by role and accessible name; prefer `screen` and `await screen.findBy*` over `waitFor`; wrap user events in `await act(async () => { fireEvent... })` as the existing Stepper tests do; never add test IDs to implementation.
Docs follow docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md: sentence-case headings, second person, present tense, short paragraphs, fenced `yaml` code blocks, no emojis.
Changeset messages are adopter-facing plain language and never name internal functions, files or variables.

decisions.choice: No transform: the Stepper already passes the full `stepsState` as rjsf `formData`, so rjsf `retrieveSchema` and ajv evaluate `if` against every earlier answer; the change only adds tests proving it.
rejected: Pre-resolving `if`/`then` in the Stepper before rendering
decisions.reason: Same evaluation path as the backend (full answer set against the step schema) and zero risk to same-step behaviour.

decisions.choice: A pure helper `expandCrossStepDependencies` in Stepper/utils.ts appends, for each `dependencies` key that is not a property of the step and not declared by another conditional branch of the step, an equivalent `{ if, then }` entry to the step's `allOf`, keeping the original `dependencies` untouched; the Stepper passes its result as the rjsf `schema`.
rejected: Injecting the earlier-step key as a hidden property of the later step
decisions.reason: rjsf skips a dependency whose key is not in the step's `properties`; `if`/`then` is evaluated against full form data, and keeping the original `dependencies` keeps ajv validation identical to the backend (NFR-2).

decisions.topic: Telling conditional and cross-step conditional fields apart
decisions.choice: Internal helpers in next/lib/schema.ts (not re-exported from next/lib/index.ts): `getConditionalPropertyNames(schema)` for the Stepper rewrite, and `getCrossStepConditions(schema)` returning `{ keys, fields }` (earlier-step names the step's conditions read, and the fields declared only under those conditions) for the Review step.
rejected: Separate walkers in Stepper and ReviewState
decisions.reason: One definition of a cross-step condition (it reads a name the step does not declare) keeps rendering and review in agreement.

decisions.topic: Review step ownership of an answer

Dropping any unresolved answer declared in any conditional branch (changes same-step Review output)
decisions.reason: The brief keeps the Review step and same-step conditions unchanged; only conditions on earlier-step answers may change what the Review step lists.

units.behaviour: Adds two internal helpers: one lists the property names a step schema declares inside conditional branches, the other tells the step's cross-step conditions (reading a property the step does not declare) apart from same-step ones.
rules: 1. `getConditionalPropertyNames(schema)` walks from `schema` into: each object item of `allOf`, `anyOf` and `oneOf` arrays; the `then` and `else` objects; and each object value of the `dependencies` object (array values are skipped); it recurses into the reached subschemas through those same keywords only.
2. For every reached subschema (never the top-level `schema` itself) whose `properties` is an object, collect its own keys (use `hasOwnProperty`, like `extractUiSchema`).
3. Never walk into `if`, `not`, `items` or any `properties` value; ignore non-object nodes.
4. Return the names in first-seen order without duplicates as `string[]`; never mutate `schema`.
5. Reuse the file's existing `isObject` guard; add a short `//` comment above each new function saying what it is used for; no TSDoc release tag and do not touch next/lib/index.ts.

6. `getCrossStepConditions(schema)` uses an inner test `declaredHere(name)`: true when `name` is an own key of `schema.properties`, or when `getConditionalPropertyNames` of `{ ...schema, dependencies: <schema.dependencies without name> }` includes `name` (use `schema` as is when `schema.dependencies` is not an object).

7. It inspects only two kinds of condition: (a) `if` nodes, meaning `schema` itself and each object item of `schema.allOf` whose `if` is an object; the condition reads the own keys of `if.properties` plus the string items of `if.required`, and its branches are `then` and `else` (objects only); (b) each own key `k` of `schema.dependencies` whose value is an object; the condition reads `k`, and its branch is that value. Array-valued dependencies and any other nesting are ignored.

8. A condition is cross-step when at least one name it reads fails `declaredHere`; those names go into `keys`. The names a branch declares are the own keys of its `properties` plus `getConditionalPropertyNames(branch)`.
9. `fields` = names declared by the branches of cross-step conditions, minus the names declared by the branches of same-step conditions, minus `keys`, minus the own keys of `schema.properties`.
10. Return `{ keys, fields }`, each in first-seen order without duplicates; a schema with only same-step conditions (or none) returns `{ keys: [], fields: [] }`; never mutate `schema`.

sites.rule: Append `export function getConditionalPropertyNames(schema: JsonObject): string[]` (rules 1-5) and then `export function getCrossStepConditions(schema: JsonObject): { keys: string[]; fields: string[] }` (rules 5-10) after `createFieldValidation`, each preceded by one blank line.

units.behaviour: Adds `expandCrossStepDependencies`, which rewrites `dependencies` keyed on an answer from another step into equivalent `allOf` if/then entries that rjsf evaluates against the full form data.
rules: 1. If `schema.dependencies` or `schema.properties` is not an object (use `isObject`), return `schema` itself (same reference).
2. Visit the own keys `k` of `schema.dependencies` in `Object.keys` order; skip `k` when it is an own key of `schema.properties` (same-step dependency, rjsf already handles it).

3. Also skip `k` when `getConditionalPropertyNames({ ...schema, dependencies: <schema.dependencies without k> })` includes `k` (a field introduced by another branch of the same step, which rjsf resolves through its dependency chain).
4. For an array value `v`: produce `{ if: { required: [k] }, then: { required: v } }`.

5. For an object value: split it into `oneOf` and the remaining keywords `rest`; when `rest` has at least one key produce `{ if: { required: [k] }, then: rest }`; when `oneOf` is an array, for each item that is an object whose `properties` is an object holding an object at `properties[k]`, produce `{ if: { properties: { [k]: item.properties[k] }, required: [k] }, then: { ...item, properties: <item.properties without k> } }`; skip other items.
6. Any other value produces nothing.

7. If nothing was produced return `schema` itself; otherwise return `{ ...schema, allOf: [...(Array.isArray(schema.allOf) ? schema.allOf : []), ...produced] }`, keeping `dependencies` unchanged so ajv validation still matches the backend.
8. Never mutate `schema` or its nested objects; build the copies with spread and Object.fromEntries/filter.
9. Add a short `//` comment above the function explaining that rjsf skips a dependency whose key is not a property of the step, so cross-step dependencies are re-expressed as if/then.

tests.expect: first render has rows `SDK name my-sdk`, `SDK token ******`, `Description d` and `Extra kept`; after rerender there is no row named /SDK name/ or /SDK token/ and no text `my-sdk`, while rows `Description d` and `Extra kept` remain

tests.name: should keep listing same-step conditional answers as before
tests.given: step 1 with boolean `isMobileSdk`; step 2 with properties `hasNotes` (boolean) and `kind` (string, enum `lib`/`app`), an `allOf` if/then on `hasNotes` const true (required ['hasNotes']) whose `then` declares `notes` (string), and `dependencies.kind.oneOf` [branch `kind` const 'lib' + `libName` (string); branch `kind` const 'app']; formState `{ isMobileSdk: true, hasNotes: false, notes: 'stale-notes', kind: 'app', libName: 'old-lib' }`
tests.expect: the texts `stale-notes` and `old-lib` are both shown (stale same-step answers are still listed, as today) and the text `app` is shown
